commits.title: Ad conversions offer the last 15 minutes each run and seven days once an hour

changes.how: queueAdConversions() (line 55) gains a parameter `since: "recent" | "week" = "week"`. Rewrite the statement to start from the connections: `from commerce.ad_connections c join commerce.orders o on o.store_id = c.store_id` with `c."on"` in the where, so no connection means no order is read. For "week" keep `o.created_at > now() - interval '7 days'`. For "recent" use: the order was created in the last 15 minutes OR has a payment captured in the last 15 minutes (`exists (select 1 from commerce.payments p where p.store_id = o.store_id and p.order_id = o.id and p.status = 'captured' and p.<the captured-at column> > now() - interval '15 minutes')`; find the column with rg -n 'capturedAt|captured_at' src/db/schema.ts near the payments table; if payments has no such column use p.updated_at, and if neither exists, stop). Everything else stays: ELIGIBLE, PURCHASED, store_is_active, the cross join of the two events, on conflict do nothing, returning 1.

queuePlatformAdConversions() (line 35): the same `since` parameter with the same two windows on its own source rows (sign-ups and first paid plans), starting from the platform's connections that are on.

Read the request body before after(): `const body = (await request.json().catch(() => ({}))) as { sweep?: unknown }; const hourly = new Date().getUTCMinutes() === 0;`. Call `queueAdConversions(hourly ? "week" : "recent")` and `queuePlatformAdConversions(hourly ? "week" : "recent")`. (The `sweep` flag is used by the last commit.)

Existing cases call queueAdConversions() with no argument and so keep the seven-day behaviour: they must pass unchanged. Add: 'recent offers an order created now and skips one created an hour ago'; 'an order created two days ago and paid now is offered by recent (its purchase event)'; 'week still offers the hour-old order'; 'with no connection on, the statement reads no order row' (rows read from commerce.orders through pg_stat_user_tables, after select pg_stat_force_next_flush()). (1) `create or replace function commerce.support_mark_email_due() returns trigger language plpgsql set search_path = ''`: `if new.author in ('agent', 'ai') then update commerce.support_conversations set email_due = true where id = new.conversation_id and not email_due; end if; return new;`. (2) `create trigger support_messages_email_due after insert on commerce.support_messages for each row execute function commerce.support_mark_email_due();`. (3) Backfill once: `update commerce.support_conversations c set email_due = true where c.anonymised_at is null and exists (select 1 from commerce.support_messages m where m.conversation_id = c.id and m.author in ('agent','ai') and m.seq > c.email_sent_seq);`. In sendReplyEmails() (line 92) add `and c.email_due` to the where of BOTH selects (the chat's at line 96 and the email and form channel's at line 113), directly after `from commerce.support_conversations c ... where`. commits.title: The three feature routes are named by the tick only when a part is due, and run only the parts that are

changes.how: Custom migration (`pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name cron_feature_due`, then `node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs`). Three functions, each `returns setof text language sql stable set search_path = ''`, each returning the NAMES of the parts that have work at p_now, one indexed exists() per part and no loop over stores: `commerce.integrations_due(p_now timestamptz default now())` with parts 'inbound' (processInboundEmails), 'workflows' (runWorkflows), 'platform_workflows' (runPlatformWorkflows), 'deliveries' (deliverDue), 'platform_deliveries' (deliverPlatformDue), 'support' (sendSupportEmails: exists a conversation with email_due), 'store_events' (processStoreEvents); `commerce.broadcasts_due(p_now)` with parts 'broadcasts' (runBroadcasts: a broadcast with status 'sending', or 'scheduled' with scheduled_for <= p_now; broadcasts_due_idx and broadcasts_sending_idx serve it), 'automations' (an enabled automation exists AND a subscriber's welcome moment or an order's delivered_at falls in the last 20 minutes; the day-delayed kinds are found on the 15-minute sweep, which is soon enough for a delay counted in days), 'review_requests' (runReviewRequests), 'gift_cards' (deliverGiftCards), 'ad_conversions' (an ad connection is on and an order was created or a payment captured in the last 15 minutes, or a queued conversion row is due), 'platform_ad_conversions' (the same for the platform's); `commerce.autopilot_due(p_now)` with parts 'plans' (runAutopilot), 'reviews' (runGoalReviews), 'events' (runEvents). For EACH part, open the runner named in brackets, find the first statement it sends when there is nothing to do (its claim or its list), and copy that statement's where clause into the exists(); wider is allowed, narrower is not. Where a runner's first statement has no index to serve it, add a partial index in this file (plain `create index if not exists`; if the table is one of orders, order_lines, visits, products, product_variants, customers, carts, cart_lines, put that index in a separate file whose first line is `-- kaizen:no-transaction` and build it `concurrently`). Then `create or replace function commerce.cron_due(...)` with the body step 3.1 gave it, changed in one place: 'autopilot', 'broadcasts' and 'integrations' are returned when the sweep is on or `exists (select 1 from commerce.<route>_due(p_now))`. Revoke as step 3.1's migration did.

At the top of run(), after the authorisation: read the body's sweep flag; `const due = sweep ? null : new Set(await dueParts("integrations"))` where dueParts(route) is a new helper in src/server/cron-runs.ts that runs `select * from commerce.<route>_due(now())` through typedRows() (route is one of three literals; build the function name from a fixed map, never from input). Run each runner only when `due === null || due.has('<its part>')`, in today's order; a skipped runner's answer is the zero value it returns today when idle. Cadence: `trackedRoute("route.integrations", 900, run)`. Make the same change in src/app/api/cron/broadcasts/route.ts (parts as named above; 900) and src/app/api/cron/autopilot/route.ts (900). Put the mapping from part name to runner in ONE exported object per route file (`const PARTS = { inbound: () => processInboundEmails(), ... }`) so the scan test can read it.

Add a case for the three gated feature routes: read each route file's PARTS keys and the newest migration that defines commerce.<route>_due; every key appears as a quoted string in that function's body, and every quoted part name in the function is a key. A runner called in the route outside PARTS fails (the route's source has no call of an imported `run*`, `send*`, `deliver*`, `process*` or `queue*` function outside the PARTS object).

This file is made by step 3.1 and does not exist before it; if it is missing, stop; if it is there, add to it and do not overwrite it. Change the empty-seed expectation: at a non-sweep minute cron_due() now returns no route at all. Add one case per part of the three functions: make that part's work due through the application's own function (schedule a broadcast for now; add an agent's support message; queue a webhook delivery; enable a welcome automation and add a subscriber; and so on), and expect cron_due() to name the route and <route>_due() to name the part.

migration.notes: Three files. (1) Generated by pnpm db:generate from src/db/schema.ts: support_conversations.email_due boolean not null default false and a partial index; not a hot table, plain index. (2) Custom: the trigger on commerce.support_messages that sets the mark, and a one-off backfill. (3) Custom: integrations_due, broadcasts_due, autopilot_due and the replaced cron_due; any index a predicate needs on a hot table goes in a fourth file that starts with `-- kaizen:no-transaction` and builds `concurrently`. Running code keeps working: columns are added with defaults, nothing is renamed or dropped, and the routes keep their addresses; until the new code is live the old routes simply run all parts when called. Ship (1) and (2) with the support commit and (3) with the last commit, never before the code that understands a rarely-called route (the 900 s cadence). CI applies it after every check passes and before the deploy (docs/ci-migrations.md); never apply it by hand. After the deploy check the Supabase security and performance advisors for project ybsozesfuxuitoacntfo and record the file's version in docs/decisions.md under Migration versions.

executor_why: Eighteen runners each need their idle statement read and turned into one indexed predicate that is never narrower than the claim, and the set-based automations query rewrites three due rules that decide who gets a marketing email.
checked_in_code: I opened the three route files, automations.ts (enabledLifecycles at line 184, dueFor at 207, runAutomations at 257), ad-conversions.ts line 55, support-email.ts lines 92 to 124 and ai-pause.ts. The finding CR-3 matches the code: the automations loop reads the store and one due query per store and kind, queueAdConversions() re-offers seven days of orders each minute, sendReplyEmails() has no due mark, and the three autopilot runners each call skipWhilePaused(). I counted 18 runners across the three routes, more than the step's text suggests, and found no existing test file for support emails (the brief creates one). The step's 'one SQL function per route' cannot hold the day-delayed automation rules cheaply each minute (the win-back query scans orders), so the brief checks the no-delay welcome each minute and leaves day-delayed kinds to the 15-minute sweep, and says so.
